steps: Boil the potatoes, covered, on medium-high for 12 to 15 minutes, until almost tender but not soft, then drain.
Peel them once cool enough to hold and prick each one all over with a fork.
Blend the onion, ginger and garlic to a smooth paste, then add the curd and blend for just a few seconds.
Heat the ghee on low, add the bay leaf, then the paste. Cover, stirring every few minutes, about 10 minutes until ghee shows at the sides.
Stir in the turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder, garam masala, sugar, salt and slit green chilli.
Add the potatoes and about 50 ml water a person, and stir into a thick gravy.
Cover tightly (foil under the lid helps) and cook on the lowest heat for 10 to 12 minutes.
Crush in the kasuri methi, add the coriander leaves and let it rest 3 to 5 minutes before serving.
note: One source used about 60 g of potatoes a person and two used 125 g; this goes with 125 g, a fair share when dum aloo is the main dish. Tomato was left out because two of the three recipes use none.
